chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) raised his head towards the sky and smiled. So it was said to him: 'O Messenger of God! We saw you raise your head towards the sky and smile.' He said: 'Yes.

I was astounded at two angels who had descended from the sky to the earth, seeking a righteous believing servant in a prayer place where he used to pray, in order to record his deeds for his day and his night. But they did not find him in his prayer place, so they ascended to the sky.

And they said: 'Our Lord! Your believing servant, so-and-so — we sought him in his prayer place to record his deeds for his day and his night, but we did not find him, and we found him in Your ropes (held by illness).'

So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Record for My servant the likes of what he used to do in his well-being, from the goodness during his day and his night, for as long as he remains in My ropes; for it is upon Me to record for him the reward of what he used to do in his well-being, when I have held him back from it.'

key_terms.حِبَالِي: My ropes — a metaphor for illness or affliction that binds and restrains a person from their normal deeds
key_terms.صِحَّة: Well-being, health — the state in which a person is able to perform their habitual acts of worship
key_terms.عَمَلَهُ: His deeds — specifically the habitual righteous acts the believer regularly performed before falling ill
key_terms.مُصَلًّى: Prayer mat or designated place of prayer — a space that a devout Muslim regularly returns to for worship

ai.seo_question: Does a sick Muslim still receive reward for acts of worship they are unable to perform due to illness?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) was moved to smile upon witnessing two recording angels who had descended to document a righteous believer's deeds, only to find him bedridden with illness. God's direct command to write full reward for the sick man reveals a profound theological principle: a sincere believer's intention and habitual practice of worship are credited even when physical incapacity prevents their fulfillment. The phrase 'in My ropes' (فِي حِبَالِي) uses the metaphor of being bound — illness as divine captivity — to emphasize that God Himself is the one who prevents the servant, thus God guarantees the continuity of reward. This teaching would have deeply comforted early Muslim communities where illness and hardship were common, assuring them that sincere devotion is never lost.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> raised his<sup>saww</sup> head towards the sky and he<sup>saww</sup> smiled. So it was said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We saw you<sup>saww</sup> raising your<sup>saww</sup> head towards the sky’. So he<sup>saww</sup> smiled and said: ‘Yes.

Isaww was astounded at two Angels who had descended from the sky to the earth, seeking a righteous believing servant in a Prayer mat which he used to pray Salaat in, in order to record his deeds for him for his day and his night. But they did not find him to be on his Prayer mat. So they ascended to the sky and said: ‘Our Lordazwj! Yourazwj believing servant, so and so, we sought him on his prayer-mat in order for us to record his deeds for him for his day and his night, but we did not come across him, and we found him in Yourazwj ropes (i.e. tied down by illness)’.
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said:

“Write down for My<sup>azwj</sup> servant the likes of what he would have doing during his well-being, from the goodness during his day and his night, for as long as he is in My<sup>azwj</sup> ropes (Illness from Me<sup>azwj</sup>), for it is upon Me<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>azwj</sup> Write for him a Recompense of what he would have done during his well-being when I<sup>azwj</sup> Reckon from him”’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once the Messenger of Allah raised his head to the heaven and smiled. He was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we saw you. Why did you raise your head to the heaven and smile?’ He then replied, ‘I was amazed when I saw two angels come down from the heaven looking for a believing, virtuous servant (of Allah) in the place he performs his prayers, so they can record his deeds of that day and night but they could not find him there. They then ascended to the heaven saying, “Lord, we looked for Your so and so believing servant in the place of his prayer to record the deeds of his day and night, but could not find him there. However, we found him (tied down) with Your ropes.’”

Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, said, “Write down for My servant (a reward) equal to that of his good deeds that he normally did in his day and night when free of (illness due to) My ropes. Do so as long as he is tied down with My ropes; I must write down for him when tied down with My ropes (suffering from illness) a reward equal to the reward of the good deeds that he did when in good health.’””
